entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Erasmus Grasser was a renowned master builder and sculptor in Munich during the early 16th century, working under the patronage of the powerful Welf dynasty. His innovative techniques and artistic flair earned him widespread recognition, and his works can still be admired in Munich's iconic Frauenkirche and St. Peter's Church.

Grasser's significance lies in his contribution to the city's architectural development, which had a lasting impact on the region's cultural identity. His legacy can be seen in the many Baroque buildings and monuments that dot the cityscape, a testament to his enduring influence.

As one of the leading artisans of his time, Grasser's work was highly sought after by the royal courts of Europe, further cementing his status as a master of his craft.

The exact dates of Grasser's birth and death remain unknown, a testament to the limited record-keeping of the time.

In the world of art and architecture, Grasser's name is still revered today, a testament to the power of human creativity to transcend time and tradition.
